projects.title: Extend cultivation
projects.body: Clear and tend another plot. More food per food worker; construction competes with gathering.

projects.title: Improve shared storage
projects.body: Enlarge the existing store while retaining its identity. Holds 120 more seasonal provisions; stock still needs tending.

projects.title: Organize the watch
projects.body: Build a small shelter, agree lookout duties and protect the landing. This is a hypothetical community watch, not a standing army.

projects.title: Share care and food preparation
projects.body: A shared working room supports care, food preparation and cooperation. Care workers are still needed every season.

after.label: Shared care and food preparation shelter

projects.title: Establish the household lane
projects.body: Widen the existing earth path and connect two new household sites. Older paths retain their identities; no stone street appears.

projects.title: Build the north household
projects.body: Build and furnish a dwelling for up to six simulated residents. Housing alone does not produce new people.

projects.title: Build the east household
projects.body: Provide a second new dwelling. Welcoming newcomers still requires food reserves, wellbeing and cooperation.

projects.title: Prepare a refuge and response route
projects.body: A low screen and a rehearsed gathering point improve protection. It is not an excavated fortification or a city wall.

projects.title: Organize seasonal meetings
projects.body: Prepare a shared meeting place for resolving disputes and coordinating work. The institution is an explicit game-design hypothesis.

projects.title: Prepare a meeting and exchange place
projects.body: An enterable room for receiving visitors and keeping bundles. Enables the optional neighbor chapter after reaching town; no automatic trade or historical market is implied.

after.label: Approach to the hypothetical meeting place

defense.title: Defend the village
defense.subtitle: The stores at dawn
defense.evidence: Fictional gameplay encounter. The raiders, tactics and injuries are authored; this is not an archaeological claim. Only the existing hypothetical wooden watch kits are used. No bows, metal weapons or army are introduced.

ui.brief: Two small raiding groups approach from the north and seek the shared stores. Keep them away until they withdraw. Losing the stores or withdrawing costs supplies. Incapacitated defenders need care afterward. There are no civilian combat groups.
ui.guide:
1  Review your named home-watch adults and equipment.
2  Deploy on clear ground; face the approach.
3  Begin, then defend the stores or intercept together.
4  Read the report, return, and recover through ordinary care and kit repair.
ui.controls: Click or drag to select · Shift adds · Right-click orders · M Move · A Advance · T Attack · H Hold · D Defend · R Withdraw · F Face · Space pause · Wheel zoom · Middle drag pan · 0 overhead · V close
ui.prep_hint: Only adults on home watch or watch practice can mobilize. Carriers, escorts, care, civic and project crews keep their commitments. Change standing watch priorities in Village before mobilizing. No season can pass during a battle.
ui.kit_hint: Preparation uses the existing chain: prepare wood in the working room, build the watch shelter, then commission wooden watch kits. Training and repair each need their own adult. These remain ordinary paid seasonal projects.
ui.cost: Mobilization: {food} provisions · {count} adults · {kits} wooden kits · readiness {readiness}/4. Existing watch facilities: {posts}.
ui.practice_note: PRACTICE · a detached copy; village and saves stay unchanged
ui.recovery: Recovery: wounded adults leave the available workforce for two fed seasons with at least two care workers. Use Village to protect food and care; kit upkeep consumes the existing prepared sets, timber and repair adult. Paid projects, homes and household history remain.
ui.saved: Battle saved, paused. Resume when ready.
ui.invalid_save: No compatible battle save in this slot.
ui.no_defenders: Assign at least one available adult to home watch first.
ui.completed: This encounter has already been resolved. Practice remains available.
ui.authority: God or the watch leader must authorize mobilization.
ui.blocked: Finish the unresolved village defense before changing work or advancing seasons.
ui.bad_order: That order has no reachable destination. Choose clear ground.
ui.waiting: Choose a command, then right-click the ground or an observed enemy.

ui.practice_save: Practice uses a detached copy and does not write your village slot.
ui.enemy_routed: The raiders lost the will to continue and withdrew.
ui.stores_taken: The raiders held the stores long enough to take supplies.
ui.watch_lost: No defenders remain able to contest the stores.
ui.withdrawn: All defenders reached withdrawal or were forced out.

ui.adoption: Explicitly adopt tactical movement, fatigue and formation rules for future battles. Your residents, paid work, equipment and previous reports remain. An unfinished older battle keeps its original rules until accepted.
ui.adopted: Village warfare enabled. Preparing or viewing does not advance the battle.

ui.unreachable_destination: No clear route reaches that destination from every selected group.
ui.no_formation_room: The selected formation has no room there. Use a column or a wider position.
ui.target_not_visible: The target is no longer visible. Advance to its last known position or choose a visible enemy.
ui.invalid_width: Choose a column or a spread formation.
ui.invalid_facing: Choose a different point to face.
ui.order_detail: Selected order: {order}. Right-click the destination; Space pauses for orders.
ui.width_hint: Column fits narrow routes. Spread gives the residents room on open ground. Congested groups queue and seek another clear route.
ui.old_battle: Finish and accept the older battle before enabling new warfare rules.

Watch aptitude {skill} · training {training}/4 · serviceable kits {kits}
Nearby {friends} allies / {enemies} enemies · protection {cover}% · ground pace {ground}%
ui.factor_note: Fatigue lowers pace and striking power. Front-facing holds and prepared positions reduce incoming damage. Local support steadies morale; flank or rear exposure increases danger.

Materials: {wood} timber · total work {work}
Project progress {progress}/{work} · allocated adults {crew} · next season {next} work
ui.fortification_weakness: Open entrances preserve village access. Raiders can go through the gap or around either end. A screen cannot defend itself.
ui.fortification_staffing: Use actual home-watch residents to Hold or Defend the inner stand. No new defenders are granted.
ui.fortification_upkeep: Uses existing watch maintenance: timber and a repair adult compete with food, care and construction. Poor watch condition removes prepared-position protection.
ui.fortification_ready: Completed and maintained: the marked inner stand provides protection while holding or defending.
ui.fortification_worn: Watch condition is too poor for prepared-position protection. Restore ordinary watch maintenance.
ui.fortification_unbuilt: The plan marks clear ground. Its screen provides no protection until the paid project is complete.
ui.warfare_missing: Enable village warfare before commissioning these defenses.
ui.plan_hint: Choose named clear ground for assembly, the threatened approach, the place to protect, reserves and fallback. Plans persist; they grant no buildings, equipment or workers.
ui.plan_saved: Defense plan saved. Review actual positions during deployment.
ui.plan_invalid: Choose an available named planning position.
ui.plan_battle_locked: Finish the unresolved battle before changing the village defense plan.
ui.saved_preparation: Village, preparations and defense plan saved.
ui.quick_hint: The same orders and battle rules run in batches. Stop & pause keeps the current fight ready to command, save or resume.
ui.modes_brief: Command personally deploys the watch and waits for you. Delegated command lets the watch leader issue valid orders. Quick resolution runs that same fight in batches.
ui.delegated_notice: The watch leader is issuing orders. Take command to give spatial orders.
ui.preparation_advantages: Paid defenses shape routes. Maintained screens protect their inner stands. Fatigue, facing, morale, training and equipment affect the same fight in every mode.
ui.threat_intro: Enable a bounded cycle of store raids, landing thefts and northern probes. Each warning leaves two full seasons to prepare. At least eight quiet seasons follow an accepted battle, with further delay during recovery or shortages.
ui.threat_quiet: The next possible warning is season {turn}. Life and paid work continue normally.
ui.threat_ready: The threat has reached the village. Prepare your watch, then choose personal command, delegated command or quick resolution. Resolve the encounter before advancing another season.
ui.threat_contact: A friendly community with completed trade or aid gave an extra season of warning. This does not identify the raiders.
ui.threat_unknown: The objective is an assessment from the approach. Enemy equipment, morale and losses are known only when observed; no numerical odds are promised.
ui.threat_recovery: Further threats wait while injured participants recover. Staff ordinary care and keep food available.
ui.threat_incident: Further threats wait while a known local incident needs preparation or recovery.
ui.threat_food: Further threats wait until reserves cover mobilization and two seasons of food for recovery.
ui.threat_watch: Further threats wait until at least one resident is available for watch duty.
ui.threat_horizon: There is not enough time left in this village chapter for a full warning and encounter.
ui.objective_held: The raiders held their objective long enough to complete the attempt.
ui.supplies_escaped: The carriers escaped with supplies from the landing.
ui.supplies_recovered: The watch stopped the carriers and recovered the supplies.
ui.deadline_held: The attackers abandoned their objective after the watch held out.
ui.threat_not_ready: Prepare through the warning seasons before mobilizing; resolve any recovery or reserve shortage shown above.
ui.warfare_guide: Review the named watch and paid preparations. Deploy on clear ground, then protect the threatened place or intercept together. Read the outcome and restore care, food and equipment afterward.
ui.objective_carrying: Supplies seized · intercept the withdrawing raiders
ui.muster_hint: Extra watch uses named adults and competes with paid construction, timber work and reserve building. Essential food, care and existing obligations remain assigned first. Requested residents become available only when the workforce can spare them; no people or equipment are granted.
ui.muster_saved: Additional watch request saved. The workforce forecast shows who can be spared.
ui.threat_enabled: Repeatable threats enabled. Quiet seasons and warning time come before the first encounter.
ui.aftermath_intro: Named residents, household recovery and equipment after each encounter.
ui.aftermath_boundary: Incapacitated residents recover through food and care. This chapter does not cause permanent combat deaths.
ui.aftermath_recovery_route: Keep food available, assign treatment care, prepare wooden sets and enable kit repair. Releasing additional watch frees residents for ordinary work.
ui.aftermath_experience_rule: Only residents whose formation struck or was hit gain experience. Each {step} engaged encounters add one watch skill point, up to the tactical skill limit.
ui.aftermath_equipment_rule: Condition describes the existing serviceable kit pool. Repair uses ordinary materials and workers, restores {gain} condition and replaces a missing set when space is available. No equipment is granted by accepting an outcome.
ui.aftermath_care_rule: Each allocated treatment worker can help {patients} residents in a fed season. Treatment shares the same finite workforce as food, building and watch duties.
ui.aftermath_command_blocked: Resolve the current battle before changing recovery work.
ui.aftermath_result: {injury} · recovery after this encounter: {recovery} treatment seasons · +{experience} watch experience
ui.aftermath_unfed: Food is short: treatment cannot advance this season.
ui.aftermath_care_short: Treatment places this season: {capacity} for {patients} recovering residents.
ui.aftermath_inactive: No longer in the active village workforce; their record remains.

projects.title: Screen the store approach
projects.body: Direct eastern approaches around two low woven sections. A maintained screen protects a watch group holding or defending the inner stand beside its open entrance. The entrance stays open for ordinary village work. Raiders can use the gap or go around either end; this is not an enclosing wall. Existing home-watch residents must hold the position. Watch maintenance uses ordinary timber and repair labor; poor watch condition removes the prepared-position benefit. These screens are fictional preparations, not an excavated defensive plan.

fortifications.evidence: Original hypothetical village preparation using the existing low woven-screen vocabulary. Location, military purpose and battle effects are gameplay interpretation, not archaeological claims. No Roman fortification, gatehouse, metalwork or enclosing wall is introduced.

encounters.title: A raid on the stores
encounters.brief: People approach the store yard from the eastern paths. They appear intent on holding the stores long enough to seize food.
encounters.stakes: Keep them away from the stores. An uncontested occupation can cost up to 16 food; defending the yard, forcing retreat or holding until they abandon the attempt protects it.

encounters.title: A theft at the landing
encounters.brief: A small raiding party approaches the landing. They may try to grab supplies and escape along their arrival route.
encounters.stakes: Protect the landing or stop the carriers before they leave. Escaping carriers can take up to 12 food; recovering the supplies protects the village reserve.

encounters.title: A probe of the northern approach
encounters.brief: Armed strangers test the northern approach. Their purpose appears to be reaching the approach and assessing the watch.
encounters.stakes: Deny the northern approach or force them to give up. This probe takes no stored food; injuries and damaged equipment still need care.

threats.evidence: Original hypothetical encounter configurations for play, not reconstructed historical raids. Approaches use authored village ground; contact reports do not identify raider affiliation.

aftermath.evidence: Original hypothetical gameplay consequences, not a reconstruction of specific wounds, medical treatments or household responses. Injuries are abstract recoverable conditions; equipment condition represents the existing serviceable kit pool.
aftermath.boundary: Combat cannot permanently kill or delete residents. Incapacitated people remain in their lifecycle, households and history and recover with food and allocated care.
